families.name: Open the session
families.meaning: Signals the start of practice and invites the listener to settle physically, such as closing or opening the eyes and taking breaths.

families.name: Settle into the body
families.meaning: Directs attention to physical posture and sensation, helping the listener feel grounded in the body.

families.name: Notice the breath
families.meaning: Points attention at the breath and its movement, such as the rise and fall of the abdomen or the nose.

families.name: Notice sounds and senses
families.meaning: Invites open attention to what is heard, seen or felt in the environment and body.
members: sounds or sensations in the body
gradually become aware of the sensations
gradually become aware of the process

families.name: Observe thoughts and emotions
families.meaning: Asks the listener to watch thoughts, feelings and mental content as they arise and pass.

families.name: Notice coming and going
families.meaning: Frames experience as transient, so the listener watches phenomena come and go without holding on.

families.name: Notice when the mind wanders
families.meaning: Acknowledges that attention drifts and gently invites the listener to notice and return.
members: lost in thought simply observe the thought

families.name: Reassure there is no failure
families.meaning: Removes pressure by telling the listener nothing is required or wrong, so they can simply be present.
members: i let go just a little bit

families.name: Invite gentle exploration
families.meaning: Softly suggests trying something or seeing what happens, keeping the tone open and curious.
members: see if you can notice the next
go just a little bit more

families.name: Rest in awareness
families.meaning: Points to the open awareness itself as the place to rest, beyond any particular object.
